correctness.rationale: For the repaired RESULT.md and SLOGAN.txt. The frozen Finding and slogan conflate the standard bipartite center–axis incidence graph (90 vertices, 180 edges) with the simple commuting graph (45 vertices, 90 edges); the latter, not either of the other graphs, is the line graph of the 30-vertex duad–syntheme Levi graph. The repair states and proves the precise bipartite double-cover relationship and the simple quotient by identifying paired labels. It also gives a checkable proof of Aut(C)=A6 using the action in Bauer et al. and the impossible Riemann–Hurwitz area 1/40 for a group of order 720 on a genus-10 curve. For an involution its isolated fixed point is a projection center. The cyclic projection group has order dividing the projection degree (5 or 6); it has order two because A6 has no order-six element. The converse follows from the projection normal form in Fukasawa–Miura–Takahashi II, Fact 2.4 and Cor. 2.5. For distinct centers, center–axis incidence is equivalent to commuting by conjugation of the projection groups and, conversely, preservation of a unique isolated fixed point. The explicit four double-transposition neighbors establish the flag adjacency and identify each center as a quadruple point of the published 45-line arrangement. A commuting pair generates the Klein four-group given by the shared duad or syntheme; the two star families are transitive under A6 and exhaust the groups. Trace-one lifts of projective involutions with spectra (1,1,-1) commute in GL3 as well, so their diagonalization shows that the three distinct centers are the triangle vertices and their axes are the opposite sides. The finite check /tmp/opencode/frozen_independent_checks.py 4 independently checked 45 labels, all 990 unordered pairs and both 15-element orbits. It does not establish the geometric premises. Frozen evidence was preserved.

value.rationale: The repaired statement provides a precise finite model for the projection centers and their incidence with fixed lines on a canonical smooth sextic, not merely a recount of multiple points. It distinguishes the different graphs and recovers adjacency and the two geometric triangle classes from duad–syntheme incidence, so researchers can use the finite model without solving for coordinates.
